method: Thesis exposure = sum over open theses of posterior x value-pool weight (mandatory infrastructure 1.0, pricing power / scarce 0.9, abundant -0.3, new risk -0.6, loses pricing power -1.0). Final = exposure x (0.5 + opportunity/100) x (1 + gap/100) x technical readiness (trend template) x attention (not-priced +15%, crowded -20%). 'ready' = passes the book's entry gate today.

picks.why: Highest composite score (7.61) and the only name carrying five thesis exposures with zero headwind: it sits on 'mandatory_infrastructure' compliance/surveillance rails for 24/7 markets (T-008, 95% posterior), coaching-agent and grid-dispatch software layers (T-005 96%, T-003 92%), plus sovereign/on-prem AI pricing power (T-002). Reality 84 against pricing 70 gives a +15 expectations gap while attention is only 33 and the name is not flagged crowded — the market is paying for the AI narrative, not for the fact that the same platform is the compliance and dispatch layer across four separate value pools.
picks.entry_condition: Already ready (stage-2, technical 88). Initiate on any pullback into rising 50-day that holds stage-2 structure; do not chase vertical extension given the 70 pricing score.
picks.key_risk: The highest-multiple name on the list — a 15-point expectations gap evaporates on one decelerating commercial-growth print, and the T-002 falsifier (security/IT budget compression to 5-7% growth) would remove its most pricing-power-heavy layer.

picks.why: The widest expectations gap in the set (+29: reality 81 vs pricing 52) with technical score 100 and 'ready' status. It holds 'gains_pricing_power' roles in endpoint inference silicon and memory under T-004 (98.3% posterior) and robot component supply under T-006 (88.7%), yet its pricing score is the second-lowest of the ready names — the cycle-stock discount is still being applied to a structurally scarce input.
picks.entry_condition: Buy now on stage-2 confirmation; scale the second tranche only after the next print confirms the reality score rather than mean-reverting.
picks.key_risk: Direct tension with its own parent thesis: T-004's next signal explicitly requires silicon to loosen relative to electrons. If Micron's next print shows memory de-tightening, the thesis is confirmed and the stock is the thing that has to give.

picks.why: Same six-layer security role set as CRWD, PANW, NET and ZS — fraud/identity, custody key management, trust attestation for local inference, all 'mandatory_infrastructure' at 81-98% posterior — but it is the only one of the group where price has not run past fundamentals (gap +3, opportunity 72, reality 75 vs pricing 72). Technical 100, stage-2, ready, attention 45 and not crowded. You get the T-002 security-as-standing-consumption exposure without the -17 to -19 gap the peers carry.
picks.entry_condition: Buy on the current stage-2 structure; add on a confirmed higher low above the 50-day.
picks.key_risk: T-002 has the lowest posterior of the infrastructure theses (81.4) and its stated falsifier — security spend compressing to 5-7% in a flat IT-budget year — hits appliance-anchored Fortinet harder than the pure-cloud peers.

picks.why: The largest raw thesis exposure in the universe (7.75) across four theses, with 'scarce' roles in power generation, electrical equipment and the SMR supply chain under T-004 at a 98.3% posterior, plus pricing power under T-003 and mandatory-infrastructure status under T-006. Attention is only 26 and it is not crowded — but reality 58 vs pricing 50 leaves only an +8 gap and the chart is basing, so the causal case is far ahead of both the tape and the current fundamental print.
picks.entry_condition: Watch only. Enter when technical_stage flips from basing to stage-2 uptrend with volume, ideally coincident with the T-004 signal (a second/third hyperscaler disclosing a power-driven schedule slip).
picks.key_risk: Narrative score 75 versus reality 58 is the clearest narrative-over-substance spread in the set; if orders convert slower than the electrons thesis implies, the stock derates while the thesis stays true.

picks.why: The purest expression of T-006's 'skilled human capital becomes scarce' and 'field labour aggregation gains pricing power' claims (88.7% posterior), reinforced by T-004's scarce mechanical EPC layer at 98.3%. Gap +12 (reality 66 vs pricing 54) with attention at 29 — the lowest-attention name among the positive-gap candidates — and narrative 59, meaning almost nobody is telling this story yet.
picks.entry_condition: Buy on the emerging-to-stage-2 transition (technical score currently 62); alternatively enter on the next specialty-contractor backlog print if management names craft labour as the binding constraint.
picks.key_risk: The named falsifier is live and near-term: BLS OES trade wage ratio flat plus shortening backlogs would kill the scarcity-rent case, and a residential construction recession would test it directly.

picks.why: Broadest-based exposure with a +5 gap and 'ready' status, anchored by T-002 enterprise security consolidation (2.28 contribution) plus scarce agentic-finance and coaching-agent layers. Uniquely, it carries an explicit -0.86 headwind — T-006 marks generic software labour as 'abundant' and T-004 flags community/ratepayer political risk on datacentre siting — which is exactly why the engine still scores it 5.99: the negative legs are already in the model and it survives them.
picks.entry_condition: Ready now, but attention is 70, the highest in the set. Size as the ballast position and add only on market-wide drawdowns rather than on strength.
picks.key_risk: The T-004 ratepayer/political-risk layer and the T-006 software-labour commoditisation are genuine value transfers away from Microsoft; if siting resistance escalates, its capex becomes stranded rather than scarce.

picks.why: Holds 'gains_pricing_power' in on-device health telemetry inference (T-005, 96% posterior) and endpoint inference silicon (T-004, 98.3%), with a +7 gap, technical 100 and ready status. The catch is that its single largest contribution (1.60) comes from T-001 — the lowest-posterior thesis in the book at 57.2% — so the market's reluctance is rational rather than blind.
picks.entry_condition: Buy now for the T-004/T-005 legs; upgrade sizing materially only if the T-001 signal fires (a top-10 issuer or card network publishing agent-transaction liability rules, or OS-level agents shipping with stored payment authority on by default).
picks.key_risk: T-001 resolving negative strands the credential-custody and delegated-authorization optionality, and T-002 separately marks baseline consumer protection as 'abundant' — leaving a hardware-cycle stock priced at 60.

picks.why: Exposure 5.86 concentrated in T-008 (2.75) at a 95% posterior, with exchange franchises and market data gaining pricing power and tokenised fund wrappers plus 24/7 compliance reporting becoming mandatory infrastructure — the cleanest listed claim on tokenised settlement rails. Attention 30, narrative 52, pricing 49: the market is assigning it no rails premium at all, which is the entire point of holding it.
picks.entry_condition: Watch. Enter on the T-008 trigger — a top-five broker or exchange going live with continuously traded tokenised equities with named market makers and published volume — combined with the technical flip out of 'emerging'.
picks.key_risk: The weakest fundamental profile in the set (reality 46, gap -3, score 4.44); if venue pluralism routes volume to crypto-native or offshore rails rather than incumbent exchanges, ICE is the disintermediated party, not the toll collector.

memo.portfolio_note: The book is deliberately built around the two theses with the highest posteriors and the most independent confirmation paths — T-004 electrons-before-silicon (98.3%) and T-005/T-008 (95-96%) — expressed through four different value pools so no single falsifier takes out more than two positions: compute/software orchestration (PLTR, MSFT), the physical power and trades layer (GEV, FIX), silicon inputs (MU), and the trust/settlement layer (FTNT, ICE, AAPL). The single biggest deliberate omission is the security complex's expensive half: NET, CRWD, PANW and ETN all carry identical or near-identical mandatory-infrastructure roles but -17 to -19 expectations gaps with pricing scores of 80-88, meaning the thesis is already in the price; FTNT is held instead as the same exposure at a +3 gap. Real concentration risk is thematic rather than sectoral — PLTR, GEV, FIX, MU and MSFT all ultimately lean on AI capex converting into physical buildout, so a capex-digestion quarter hits five of eight names together, and PLTR plus MU together carry the two widest expectations gaps and therefore the most reflexive downside. The list changes if: (a) the FY2027 IT-budget reconciliation shows security spend compressing to 5-7%, which cuts FTNT and downgrades MSFT and PLTR's T-002 leg; (b) Micron's next print shows genuine silicon de-tightening, which confirms T-004 for GEV/FIX while removing the reason to own MU; (c) the T-001 liability-rule signal fires, which promotes AAPL from a hardware-cycle position to a core holding; or (d) GEV's chart flips to stage-2, at which point it becomes the largest single position given its 7.75 exposure and 26 attention score.
